relevance_note: Case report of one woman with a heterozygous TNFAIP3 variant ("A novel heterozygous variant was identified in TNFAIP3; ENST00000237289 c.1906C>T"), plus her two affected children and her father described in relation to her.
method_note: Hand-extracted from the text; no tables carry patient data (supplementary Table S1 is gnomAD residue statistics only, no patients). Labels: the proband has no own label ('the proband', 'the index case' are role words), so rule 5 'patient'; relatives by rule 2: the children are stated as 'a girl' and 'a boy' (sex stated), labelled 'daughter of patient' and 'son of patient'; 'father of patient' from 'the father of the index case'. No variant rows for the relatives: the paper says only that 'Genetic analysis of family members found segregation with the inflammatory clinical phenotypes (Figure 1A)' without naming who was tested or who carries the variant (the pedigree/Sanger results are only in Figure 1A); the father 'is looked after by another hospital' and is not stated to have been tested. Proband inheritance therefore not reported. Relatives have is_proband false (rule 5). Age at diagnosis of the proband is the age of the clinical AOSD diagnosis (21); age at HA20 genetic diagnosis is not given. Vital status not stated explicitly (left not reported). Normal investigations: 'blood and urinary cultures were negative' recorded as positive cultures excluded; 'abdominal ultrasound showed no obvious intraabdominal pathology' recorded in the paper's own scope (intraabdominal pathology excluded), not as exclusion of GI inflammation; ANA, RF and ACPA negative recorded as excluded features, but the composite checklist item 'autoantibodies (ANA/other)' left not reported (narrow-vs-broad rule). Father: only a diagnosis of early onset RA is given; checklist 'arthritis or arthralgia' marked observed from that diagnosis. Functional results (Western blot, p65, cytokines, ASC specks) are for the proband only; the paper notes she was on tocilizumab at the time of testing. n_patients_reported left null: the authors do not state a count of variant carriers. No contradictions found.

functional_evidence_statement.value: Patient cDNA showed a mutant allele with deletion of exon 8; loss of transcript by nonsense-mediated decay with A20 haploinsufficiency confirmed by Western blot; greater p65 phosphorylation in LPS-stimulated patient monocytes (not statistically significant); significantly increased IL-1beta and IL-18 from patient PBMC after LPS/ATP; significantly higher serum ASC specks than healthy controls
span: The patient’s cDNA produced a mutant allele containing deletion of exon 8
Loss of transcript by nonsense-mediated decay resulting in A20 haploinsufficiency was confirmed by Western blot
greater percentage of patient monocytes became p65 positive compared with monocytes from healthy controls. However, this did not reach a statistical significance
The production of IL-1β and IL-18 was found to be significantly increased in the patient’s PBMC compared with healthy controls
patient serum contained significantly higher numbers of ASC specks compared with our healthy control range
